Highest-precedence classification in gen-ledger: overrides the auto 'flagged: verify' from the Layer-2 read diff. deep_verified stays as the live layers report it (these do not diff clean vs Jellyfin by design). Sourced from the parity-triage workflow verdicts (parity/triage-findings.json) + the roadmap synthesis, minus the ops since fixed (Filters2 WI-2, Collections add/remove WI-6, Images Size WI-1).
last_verified: 2026-08-29 batch A3 (stale seed rows + the MediaStream probe-value residual): the 'instance/probe-noise' framing on GET /Items/{itemId} and /PlaybackInfo was disproven by cross-probing both containers' ffprobe binaries (byte-identical output) and replaced with a bitrate-only jellyfin-bug entry; the three 2026-08-11 'verified' seeds for DisplayPreferences, LiveTv/Timers/Defaults and MusicGenres were deleted after the underlying server bugs were fixed, so those rows now earn deep_verified from a live probe instead of a sentence.  2026-08-29 batch A4 (sweep single-item alignment), + reviewer-fix pass: /Items/Root deep-verified via reads.py (the playlists plugin folder is parented to the user root, so ChildCount is 4 as upstream); the ExternalIdInfos / MetadataEditor / RemoteImages / RemoteImages-Providers rows are probed by kind-fanned, Path-correlated reads.py rows and their remaining diffs are the four accepted provider-lineup entries recorded here, with the MusicBrainz ordering, the hollow TVDB/TMDB id fields, the missing TMDB Season/Episode image providers and the missing remote-image language filter all fixed in the server. The reviewer-fix pass added the /Items/Root structural note above and closed the stored-kind regressions the PlaylistsFolder switch had orphaned (CanDelete, ICollectionFolder classification, the playlists-library browse).  2026-08-30 batch C2 reviewer-fix pass: the Apply row's `body-diff`/deep_verified verdict was WITHDRAWN - it had been won inside a seconds-wide window while the suite's own library scan was in flight, and the two servers do not hold the same item once that scan lands. The journey now forces the scan and waits for it, the row is red on `unlocked_after_scan`, and the scan-overwrites-Identify divergence is recorded on its own row with the C# citation and the un-defer path. The same pass demoted that row's method from `body-diff` to `property` (it compares a named projection of the read-back, not a body), paired every fetcher-gate assertion in reads.py with a positive control so a musicbrainz.org 503 can no longer satisfy one, stopped a Ferrofin 5xx being laundered into a dropped leg, and fixed the `RefreshLibrary` scheduled task to await its scan (it reported itself finished in 0 ms with the scan still writing, where v10.11.8 `RefreshMediaLibraryTask.ExecuteAsync` awaits `ValidateMediaLibraryInternal`). That last one is FIXED, so it earns a code comment and a unit test rather than a classifications row that would label a now-correct row open work; the existing `GET /ScheduledTasks` instance note stands unchanged.  The same pass also REVERTED a metadata change monitor a previous agent had half-built on this branch (an `ItemRefreshRow` projection, a `RefreshState` read once per scan and then never consulted, and an unconditional `DateLastSaved` stamp on every save). Half of that port is worse than none of it: reading the stamps without gating on them costs a query per scan and changes nothing, and the stamp alone moves `Etag` and the `minDateLastSaved` filter on every DTO in the API without the perf run that change is owed. It is an OPEN WORK ITEM, not an accepted state: the three-step un-defer path is on the `POST /Items/RemoteSearch/Apply/{itemId}` row below and repeated as a code comment at the ungated call site (crates/ferrofin-core/src/library_scan.rs, `fetch_local_nfo`), so it is findable from either end.

GET /Albums/{itemId}/Similar.classification: flat-provider methodology (SET-GATED, order not gateable). Seeds of this kind take the C# FLAT provider: one `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [<kind>], EnableGroupByMetadataKey = false, EnableTotalRecordCount = true, OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Ascending)] }` — identical in v10.11.8 (built inline at LibraryController.cs:791-801) and in master (SeriesSimilarItemsProvider.cs:49, MusicAlbumSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, AudioSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, LiveTvProgramSimilarItemsProvider.cs:89). Ferrofin runs the same query and, as of this pass, the same `Random` order. IT BRIEFLY DID NOT: batch A2 first shipped `SortName` here, which is not cosmetic — at limit < |candidates| a fixed order returns a DIFFERENT ITEM, measured on the loop pair as `/Items/{audio}/Similar?limit=1` answering 'Artist 01 Album 01 Track 02' on five consecutive Ferrofin calls while Jellyfin alternated Track 02 / Track 03. That divergence is now closed in the server (`similar_items_manager.rs::flat_similar`, unit test `the_flat_provider_orders_random_not_by_name`), not papered over. WHAT THIS LEDGER ROW DOES AND DOES NOT GATE: `Random` on both sides means the ORDER can never be diffed by any probe, and neither can a page narrower than the candidate pool — parity_diff aligns arrays by Path>Name>Id, so a reordered Items array returns 0 diffs and always will. The reads.py leg therefore pins `limit=1000`, far above the fixture's pool, where the answer is the whole candidate set and so fully determined; what is gated there is the SET, TotalRecordCount and every per-item DTO field. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. GREEN BUT VACUOUS ON THE CURRENT FIXTURE — read this row as 'no divergence detected', not as 'verified'. `suite/perf/gen-fixtures.sh` gave each of the 3 albums a UNIQUE music genre, so the candidate universe is empty by construction on BOTH servers and the leg diffs `{"Items": [], "TotalRecordCount": 0}` against itself. The fixture is changed (two of the three artists now share a genre) but that only takes effect at the campaign's final wipe-and-provision; until that sweep runs, the album matching itself is covered by the `an_album_seed_matches_albums_sharing_a_genre_only` unit test (two albums sharing a genre, a same-genre track that must NOT come back because IncludeItemTypes is [MusicAlbum] alone, and the ExcludeArtistIds leg with a positive control). A real Ferrofin bug found behind this row IS fixed and verified live: album Genres/Studios/PremiereDate are inherited from the album's Audio children (C# AlbumMetadataService + MetadataService.UpdateGenres/UpdateStudios/UpdatePremiereDate); Ferrofin aggregated only album-artist and year, so every album had `Genres: []` and was unreachable by the Genres= query this endpoint issues. After the fix, F album Genres/PremiereDate/ProductionYear match J exactly (Jazz/Rock/Ambient, 2022-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z, 2022).

GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Ferrofin returns 0 rows where Jellyfin returns 2. The scorer half is fixed — the seed's kind now selects the C# provider shape (`MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider` is a flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [MusicArtist] }`, and an EMPTY Genres/Tags pair is not a predicate, so an untagged artist must match every other artist; covered by the `an_untagged_artist_seed_still_matches_every_other_artist` unit test). What still blocks it is the item-UNIVERSE divergence, not the similarity code: Ferrofin materializes MusicArtist as a parentless by-name row with a NULL TopParentId, and every user-scoped `InternalItemsQuery` is scoped to the user's views via `TopParentId IS NOT NULL` (item_repository.rs `scope_to_user_libraries`, the port of C# `AddUserToQuery`), so no artist is reachable by any query that does not name it by id. Detector, both servers: `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=MusicArtist` -> F 0, J 3, while `/Artists?userId=<u>` returns all 3 on both, and adding `&ids=<artistId>` makes the same query return the row on Ferrofin. Same root cause as the MusicArtist/Folder/TvChannel/UserView rows missing from GET /Items/Suggestions. Un-defer path: give the MusicArtist by-name row a TopParentId (Jellyfin's artist rows are physical folder items under the music library, which is why they survive `AddUserToQuery`) — this changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it needs its own change with the perf gate, not a ride-along. ORDERING, for the record: this endpoint's provider orders `Random` on both servers (MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50 / v10.11.8 LibraryController.cs:801) and Ferrofin now emits `Random` too, so when the universe bug is fixed the reads leg must stay pinned at a limit above the candidate pool — the ORDER is not gateable by any probe, since parity_diff aligns arrays by key.

GET /Items/Suggestions.classification: open-work (NOT accepted). The old text ('Random, so the set is non-deterministic') was only half true and it hid two real divergences. Random here PERMUTES but does not change the set: `SuggestionsController` runs ONE query (`OrderBy = [(Random, Descending)]`, Recursive, mediaType/type, IsVirtualItem=false) and Ferrofin's handler is a line-for-line port, so at `limit >= |universe|` the answer is fully determined and parity_diff aligns Items by Path. The probe was the problem: `limit=10` sampled 10 of 552 at random and could never diff. It is now eight legs: seven pinned at a full limit (per type), where Random only permutes and the whole body IS diffed, plus one narrow startIndex/limit leg. That narrow leg is the one place a projection is applied — a page of 3 out of 500 Random-ordered rows draws a different triple per call on BOTH servers (measured: three consecutive calls, three different triples each side), so it compares StartIndex, TotalRecordCount and the page length only. Diffing its Items would pin this row red forever and destroy its ability to signal when the two real divergences below are fixed; the projection is scoped to that leg alone and nothing was added to parity_diff.VOLATILE. Two causes remain, BOTH owned by other rows and deliberately left visible here rather than filtered out of the probe: (1) ITEM UNIVERSE — Ferrofin's recursive user-root universe has no MusicArtist, Folder, TvChannel or UserView rows (F 552 vs J 561 unfiltered; per type F 0 vs J 3/3/2/1), the same parentless-by-name/TopParentId cause as GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar; detector `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&limit=100000`, which shows the identical 9-row delta, so it is not this handler's bug. (2) PER-ITEM DTO FIELDS — MediaSources[].Name/Bitrate, MediaStreams[].BitRate (a constant 192000 offset), LocalizedLanguage, Level/IsAVC/Width/Height: the same set already classified on GET /Items/{itemId} as independent-probe noise, inherited here because Suggestions returns full item DTOs. Narrowing the compare to hide either would be the dishonest green; the row stays red until they are fixed on their own rows. The multi-leg probe no longer skips a leg whose servers disagree on status: a status divergence (or a body that is not 200-with-JSON on both sides) is recorded as a mismatch, which is the whole point of keeping the type=MusicArtist and type=TvChannel legs. UNIVERSE GAP, re-measured 2026-08-29 and WIDER than first written: LiveTvProgram belongs on the missing-kind list too — `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=LiveTvProgram` returns 338 rows on Jellyfin and 0 on Ferrofin, while `/LiveTv/Programs` returns the guide on both (F 19200, J 338). The knock-on is visible on a THIRD row: GET /Genres is red only because Jellyfin's genre list carries `News`, the XMLTV guide's programme genre, which Ferrofin's genre list cannot see for the same reason. One fix (give the by-name/programme rows a TopParentId so `scope_to_user_libraries` stops filtering them out) closes /Artists Similar, these Suggestions legs and the /Genres row together; it changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it is its own change WITH the perf gate.

GET /Items/{itemId}.classification: jellyfin-bug (bitrate only): Ferrofin reports MediaStreams[video].BitRate as container-minus-other-streams and MediaSources[].Bitrate as the stream sum; Jellyfin 10.11.8 falls the video stream back to formatInfo.BitRate verbatim (ProbeResultNormalizer.cs:978-987) and then InferTotalBitrate(true) (PRN.cs:259-264), which double-counts the audio. Measured on the fixture: the file is 775053 B / 1.023 s = 6,060,832 bps, so Jellyfin's MediaSources[].Bitrate of 6,253,020 exceeds what the file physically contains, while Ferrofin's 6,061,020 matches ffprobe's own format.bit_rate. Upstream fixed this itself in PR #16248 (master PRN.cs:979-991 comments that formatInfo.BitRate is the container, not the video bitrate) and Ferrofin ports the fixed form. Kept per 'don't port Jellyfin bugs'. OWNER CALL PENDING: porting 10.11.8's arithmetic instead would make this row body-diffable at the cost of being wrong. NOTE: the previous 'instance/probe-noise' text on this row was DISPROVEN in batch A3 — running both containers' ffprobe binaries over the same file gives byte-identical JSON (7.1.4 vs 7.1.3-Jellyfin), and ffprobe emits no per-stream bit_rate at all. The five other residuals it covered were real server bugs and are fixed: MediaSources[].Name now ports BaseItem.GetMediaSourceName (file stem, not item.Name); codec_tag_string binds the correct 10.11.8 JSON key (the trailing-'?' typo is master-only); Level/IsAVC are set on every stream and subtitle Width/Height default to 0, matching C#'s non-nullable probing DTO; LocalizedLanguage is no longer serialized (off-contract, the cause of schema_valid:false); and the People[].Role read projection no longer NULLIFs the empty string C# always emits.

GET /Items/{itemId}/Ancestors.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): with both containers on the same data dir the ancestor rows now align by Path and every field matches except two, BOTH on the UserRootFolder hop. (1) ChildCount J=4 H=3 — UserRootFolder.GetEligibleChildrenForRecursiveChildren (UserRootFolder.cs:96-102) concatenates LibraryManager.RootFolder.VirtualChildren, which is the PlaylistsFolder CreateRootFolder adds at {data}/playlists (LibraryManager.cs:1090-1120); Ferrofin stores that folder parentless and has no AggregateFolder root with virtual children, so the user root counts 3 libraries instead of 4 and /Items?parentId=<root> returns 3. (2) PrimaryImageAspectRatio present on Jellyfin, absent on Ferrofin — FolderImageProvider generates a collage for the user root (Supports() rejects only PhotoAlbum/MusicAlbum and IsTopParent folders); Ferrofin ports CollectionFolderImageProvider (the library tiles) but not FolderImageProvider, so the user root has no Primary image. Un-defer path: port UserRootFolder's virtual-children concat (the direct-children query AND the ChildCount prefetch) and FolderImageProvider. The previous text on this row claimed the residual was '/config-vs-/data path-derived ids only'; that was measurably false — the ids were already identical on both servers and only the Path STRING differed, which is the array align key, so no field was ever compared.

GET /Items/{itemId}/PlaybackInfo.classification: jellyfin-bug (bitrate only): Ferrofin reports MediaStreams[video].BitRate as container-minus-other-streams and MediaSources[].Bitrate as the stream sum; Jellyfin 10.11.8 falls the video stream back to formatInfo.BitRate verbatim (ProbeResultNormalizer.cs:978-987) and then InferTotalBitrate(true) (PRN.cs:259-264), which double-counts the audio. Measured on the fixture: the file is 775053 B / 1.023 s = 6,060,832 bps, so Jellyfin's MediaSources[].Bitrate of 6,253,020 exceeds what the file physically contains, while Ferrofin's 6,061,020 matches ffprobe's own format.bit_rate. Upstream fixed this itself in PR #16248 (master PRN.cs:979-991 comments that formatInfo.BitRate is the container, not the video bitrate) and Ferrofin ports the fixed form. Kept per 'don't port Jellyfin bugs'. OWNER CALL PENDING: porting 10.11.8's arithmetic instead would make this row body-diffable at the cost of being wrong. Same root cause and same batch-A3 fixes as GET /Items/{itemId}; the 'instance/probe-noise' text previously on this row was equally disproven.

GET /Items/{itemId}/Similar.classification: instance/methodology (PROPERTY-VERIFIED, NOT body-diffed — the ledger counts and lists this row separately from the deep-verified ones; status codes, the empty short-circuits, the count invariant and the candidate rule are what is gated, by the reads.py `similar_invariants` probe, and each of the three property rows now issues its OWN alias rather than all three probing /Movies). Two independent reasons a movie seed's item array cannot diff, both measured on the loop pair. (1) ORDER: Jellyfin 10.11.8 sets `OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, Ascending)]` (v10.11.8 LibraryController.cs:801); five identical calls at limit=12 returned five different SETS, because limit < |universe|. (2) ALGORITHM: 10.11.8 builds ONE flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags }`, while Ferrofin ports upstream master's weighted `MovieSimilarItemsProvider` (genre 10 / tag 5 / studio 5 / director 50 / actor+guest-star 15, MovieSimilarItemsProvider.cs:27-31) plus its phase-2 `IsMovie = true, IsPlayed = false` + ConfigureUserAccess pass. Measured at limit=1000: Jellyfin 299 items, Ferrofin 432, and Jellyfin's set is a STRICT SUBSET of Ferrofin's (onlyJ=0); the 133 extras each share a studio and/or a person with the seed and no genre — master's dimensions exactly. *** OWNER DECISION PENDING (NOT an agent-granted acceptance): running master's scorer against a 10.11.8 oracle is a deliberate ALGORITHM divergence on three ops, and CLAUDE.md reserves additions to the accepted-divergence list to the owner. The engineering case for keeping master is the repo's 'do not port Jellyfin bugs' rule — 10.11.8 additionally over-returns by 4 at every limit (measured 1/3/5/12/50 -> 5/7/9/16/54) because `BaseItemRepository.PrepareFilterQuery` (v10.11.8:1427-1430) adds 4 when `EnableGroupByMetadataKey` and never trims back, while Ferrofin honours limit exactly as master's `.Take(requestedLimit)` does — but the call is the owner's, and reverting to 10.11.8's flat query would make these three rows body-diffable at a pinned wide limit. *** WHAT IS VERIFIED LIVE instead of a body diff (every fact computed per server and then compared): status 200, StartIndex 0, TotalRecordCount == len(Items), the seed is never returned, every Type is in the C# IncludeItemTypes, the page is full, len(Items) <= limit+4 (the named Jellyfin quirk is the ONLY slack), an unknown seed is 404 on both, a nil seed is 200-empty on both, an Episode seed short-circuits empty on both, the five aliases agree as sets at limit=1000, and `obeys_own_candidate_rule` — each server's answer is re-derived independently from the DTO fields under ITS OWN documented algorithm (Jellyfin: every row shares a genre or tag with the seed, which 200 of the 500 fixture movies violate; Ferrofin: the answer equals master's weighted model's top-N IN ORDER by score desc, then Ferrofin's OWN SortName/Id tiebreak — master has no tiebreak at all, `MovieSimilarItemsProvider.cs:189-195` is `OrderByDescending(score)` alone, so that clause pins Ferrofin's rule, which is strictly more determined than the C#'s). The person dimension is matched as (Name, PersonType) pairs because that is what a `PeopleId` IS — 'the Peoples table has one row per (Name, PersonType)' (PeopleRepository.cs:47) — which is exactly what both master's `PeopleId` join and Ferrofin's SQL compute. Negative controls run 2026-08-29: the Ferrofin clause fails on a reversed order and on 12 arbitrary movies, the Jellyfin clause fails on 12 movies outside its universe. NOT REACHED BY ANY PARITY LAYER, and unit-covered instead: the phase-2 filters — the lab has zero played movies and one all-libraries user, so `IsPlayed = false` and ConfigureUserAccess are exercised only by `a_played_movie_is_not_suggested_to_the_user_who_played_it`, `a_library_the_user_cannot_access_contributes_nothing`, `a_blocked_media_folder_hides_its_rows` and `the_access_filter_does_not_starve_the_page` in similar_items_manager.rs. Three real Ferrofin bugs this row used to hide were fixed in the same pass: an unknown seed returned 200-empty instead of 404, a nil seed returned 400 instead of the C# root-folder fallback, and the no-limit default was 10 instead of C#'s `limit ?? 50` (SimilarItemsManager.cs:93).

GET /Libraries/AvailableOptions.classification: expected-extension (SupportedImageTypes + the fetcher lists): Ferrofin compiles in TheTVDB, FanArt, Open Subtitles and IntroSkipper, which the lab's stock Jellyfin 10.11.8 does not ship (GET /Plugins there lists only AudioDB and MusicBrainz). They therefore appear as extra ImageFetchers/MetadataFetchers rows, and — because SupportedImageTypes is the flattened union of every compiled image provider's GetSupportedImages (ProviderManager.cs:706-714) — their image types (Art/Disc/Banner) widen that list beyond Jellyfin's. The 2026-08-11 'verified' text this replaces was false: sweep already recorded 15 extra / 39 mismatch / 2 missing paths and schema_valid:false on this row. Fixed in batch A3: DefaultImageOptions is now the verbatim TypeOptions.DefaultImageOptions table (order included, [] for unnamed types); SupportedImageTypes is derived from the providers instead of a hardcoded 11-element enum dump; isNewLibrary now drives DefaultEnabled; and SimilarItemProviders (post-10.11.8, additionalProperties:false) is no longer serialized. OPEN WORK, not accepted: upstream's 'Screen Grabber' (VideoImageProvider, Order 100, [Primary]) is still unported — Ferrofin owns the capability (MediaEncoder::extract_video_image) but does not register the provider, so it is deliberately absent from the list rather than advertised hollow.

GET /LiveTv/GuideInfo.classification: instance: property-verified by reads.py (guide_info_invariants), not asserted. The old note claimed the 'now .. now+7d' window matched Jellyfin; it did not — GuideManager.GetGuideInfo is now .. now + GetGuideDays() (LiveTvOptions.GuideDays clamped 1..14, default 7) and Ferrofin's handler took no state, so it answered a hardcoded 7 days whatever the dashboard was set to (measured: GuideDays=14 gave J +14d, F +7d). Ported. What is compared now: window length in seconds, whole-day-ness, now-relativity, UTC tick wire format, and that both bounds come from ONE UtcNow. Excluded: the instant itself, and the fraction's DIGIT COUNT — Utf8JsonWriter's FFFFFFF trims trailing zeros, so both servers emit 5, 6 or 7 digits depending on the instant (sampled 60x each).

NOT REACHED BY ANY PARITY LAYER, and unit-covered instead: the phase-2 filters — the lab has zero played movies and one all-libraries user, so `IsPlayed = false` and ConfigureUserAccess are exercised only by `a_played_movie_is_not_suggested_to_the_user_who_played_it`, `a_library_the_user_cannot_access_contributes_nothing`, `a_blocked_media_folder_hides_its_rows` and `the_access_filter_does_not_starve_the_page` in similar_items_manager.rs. Ferrofin ships TVDB compiled in; stock 10.11.8 does not. Evidence: `git grep -l ": IExternalId" v10.11.8` lists 19 classes (Imdb, ImdbPerson, Imvdb, AudioDb x4, MusicBrainz x7, Tmdb{BoxSet,Movie,Person,Series}, Zap2It) and NOT ONE Tvdb — upstream's TVDB support is the out-of-tree jellyfin-plugin-tvdb. Ferrofin advertises exactly ONE TVDB field, `TheTVDB Numerical`/`Tvdb`/`Series`, and it is BACKED: `resolve_tmdb_id` resolves a series through TMDB `/find?external_source=tvdb_id` (provider_manager.rs, gated on `TmdbKind::Series`) and the fanart.tv series lookup is keyed by TVDB id. The Season/Episode/Movie/Person TVDB fields Ferrofin used to advertise were HOLLOW — nothing read them — and were deleted in this batch rather than classified. `Comic Vine`/`ComicVine`/`Person` is a Ferrofin addition: 10.11.8 has no ComicVine IExternalId (same `git grep` evidence as above). It is backed — `external_ids.rs::book_urls` renders a Comic Vine "Links" entry for `Book | Person` items carrying the id — and Ferrofin ships a books provider (`ferrofin-providers/src/books.rs`, which also writes GoogleBooks/ISBN from OPF metadata). The Book-kind fields (ComicVine/GoogleBooks/ISBN) are the same divergence but are NOT measurable in this fixture, which has no Book items — see the residual note for batch A4. Measured live on the A4 pair (Ferrofin 18196 / Jellyfin 10.11.8 18197), same path-derived item id on both, twice: Movie, Season, Episode, MusicAlbum and Audio now diff byte-identical INCLUDING ORDER (the MusicBrainz descriptor block was registered out of order and is fixed); only Series and Person differ, by exactly the two rows above. Every other field of the editor body (Countries, Cultures, ParentalRatingOptions, ContentTypeOptions) diffs clean.

GET /Items/{itemId}/RemoteImages/Provide.classification: accepted-divergence (provider lineup, 1 entry): Ferrofin compiles fanart.tv in as a remote image provider and stock Jellyfin 10.11.8 does not — its ten concrete `IRemoteImageProvider` implementors are AudioDb{Album,Artist}, Omdb, StudioImages and Tmdb{BoxSet,Movie,Person,Episode,Season,Series} (`git grep -l IRemoteImageProvider v10.11.8`, minus the interface, the two Manager files and the two test files), with no fanart provider in tree — fanart is an out-of-tree plugin, and the only `fanart` strings in 10.11.8 are filename patterns and NFO tags. So a Movie, Series, MusicArtist or MusicAlbum lists one extra `FanArt` entry. Measured live on the A4 pair over seven path-correlated kinds: dropping that single entry makes the arrays equal field-for-field INCLUDING `SupportedImages` and order. The real bug that was hiding under this flag IS FIXED, not classified: Ferrofin had no `TmdbSeasonImageProvider` arm at all (a Season offered NO providers) and no `TmdbEpisodeImageProvider` (an Episode offered only OMDb, `Order = 90`); both are ported, ordered TMDB-first per `IHasOrder`, and Season/Episode/Audio/Person now diff clean.

GET /Items/{itemId}/RemoteImages.classification: accepted-divergence (provider lineup): two documented lineup facts, no server bug left. (1) `Providers` is built from `GetRemoteImageProviderInfo(item)` and narrowed ONLY by `type`, never by `providerName` (v10.11.8 RemoteImageController.cs:92-99) — so every leg, scoped or not, carries Ferrofin's extra `FanArt` entry (see `GET /Items/{itemId}/RemoteImages/Providers`). (2) On the UNSCOPED leg, fanart.tv adds its own images and Jellyfin's OMDb adds one Primary that Ferrofin cannot (upstream bakes an OMDb key at OmdbProvider.cs:257; Ferrofin's OMDb is inert without FERROFIN_OMDB_KEY — CLAUDE.md 'Current scope'). What this row now PROVES: on `providerName=TheMovieDb`, `Images` and `TotalRecordCount` are byte-identical INCLUDING ORDER on all four legs measured live on the A4 pair (default 138/138, includeAllLanguages=true 391/391, type=Logo 7/7, series 0/0). That is the fix this batch landed — Ferrofin was serving 497 images where 10.11.8 served 139, unfiltered and unsorted, because `ProviderManager.GetImages`' preferred-language filter and `OrderByLanguageDescending` were never ported (`RemoteImageQuery.include_all_languages` was read by nothing).

GET /Items/Root.classification: accepted-divergence (structural: where the playlists plugin folder hangs). The row's own body diffs CLEAN and this op stays deep-verified — the note records a difference that shows on NEIGHBOURING surfaces, so it is not invisible. Upstream builds TWO roots: the AggregateFolder at `ApplicationPaths.RootFolderPath` and the UserRootFolder at `DefaultUserViewsPath`. `LibraryManager.CreateRootFolder()` (v10.11.8 Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/LibraryManager.cs:838-887) sets `folder.ParentId = rootFolder.Id` where `rootFolder` is the AGGREGATE folder, then `rootFolder.AddVirtualChild(folder)`; the UserRootFolder only picks it up at read time via `GetEligibleChildrenForRecursiveChildren` = `base.Children.ToList()` + `list.AddRange(LibraryManager.RootFolder.VirtualChildren)` (UserRootFolder.cs) — an APPEND, and `UserRootFolder.IsPreSorted => true`, so it is never re-sorted. Ferrofin has no AggregateFolder row and instead stores the playlists folder as a real DB child of the UserRootFolder. That is deliberate: `ChildCount` is served by the grouped child-count query over `ParentId`, so a row that is not a real child is a row the count cannot see — which is the bug this batch fixed (Ferrofin reported 3 where upstream reports 4). TWO OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCES, both measured live on the A4 pair (Ferrofin 18196 / Jellyfin 10.11.8 18197), twice: (1) ORDER on `GET /Items?parentId=<userRootFolderId>` (non-recursive — C# `folder.GetChildren(user, true)`, ItemsController.cs:526-528). Ferrofin sorts the folder inline by SortName: Movies, Music, Playlists, Shows. Jellyfin appends it: Movies, Music, Shows, Playlists. The four items are otherwise identical field-for-field. (2) `ParentId` on the playlists row itself: Ferrofin writes the user root (`e9d5075a…`), Jellyfin writes the aggregate root (`f27caa37…`). Masked in the harness by the pre-existing VOLATILE `ParentId` entry, recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered. NOT an adoption hazard, verified in the C#: on swap-back, Jellyfin's `CreateRootFolder()` sees `!folder.ParentId.Equals(rootFolder.Id)` and repairs the column at startup before serving, and even before that repair the row cannot be double-counted — `Folder.AddChildren` accumulates into a `Dictionary<Guid, BaseItem>` and `GetChildren` returns `result.Values`, so a row reachable both as a DB child and as a VirtualChild collapses to one entry (Folder.cs:1348-1436). ChildCount stays 4 either way. `GET /Library/MediaFolders` — the endpoint jellyfin-web actually uses for this list, and a separately deep-verified row — is UNAFFECTED and matches upstream exactly, including the folder's `CollectionType: playlists` and `CanDelete: false`. Closing this properly means giving Ferrofin a real AggregateFolder row plus a virtual-child seam the count service understands; matching only the ordering would mean special-casing the shared item query on the root parent, which is a perf-gated hot path. Filed as open work, not as an accepted end state.

POST /Items/RemoteSearch/Apply/{itemId}.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Apply itself is correct on both servers; what diverges is whether its effect SURVIVES a library scan. Measured on the lab pair, reproduced three times: Apply into a library with every "Metadata downloaders" box cleared leaves Movie 0497 identical on both (ProductionYear null, Genres [], Studios [], ProviderIds {Tmdb: 603}, and Name / RunTimeTicks / ImageTags / People untouched) - the `unlocked` half of the journey's evidence matches field for field. The journey then runs the library scan to completion on each server and reads the item back again: Jellyfin holds the cleared state, Ferrofin reverts to ProductionYear 2020 / Genres [Comedy, SciFi] / Studios [Ferrofin Studios], re-applied from /media/synth/movies/Movie 0497 (2020)/movie.nfo. That is the whole of the row's `unlocked_after_scan` diff. CAUSE: upstream gates every local metadata reader on a change monitor - v10.11.8 MediaBrowser.XbmcMetadata/Providers/BaseNfoProvider.cs `HasChanged` is `nfoLastWriteTimeUtc - item.DateLastSaved > TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)`, and MetadataService.GetProviders (:613-708) returns an EMPTY provider list when no provider reports a change, so a scan over an item saved more recently than its sidecar runs no providers and merges nothing. Ferrofin's scan re-derives every item from disk on every pass: library_scan.rs calls `fetch_local_nfo` unconditionally for any unlocked row and `save_scanned_items` writes the result over the stored columns. UN-DEFER PATH, and why it is not a ride-along: the port needs three things together - (1) populate `BaseItems.DateLastSaved` on every save (nothing writes it today; the column exists and is bound, but only ever from an entity carrying None), (2) gate `fetch_local_nfo` / `fetch_remote_metadata` on the sidecar-vs-DateLastSaved comparison, and (3) a third scan-upsert variant that PRESERVES the provider-supplied columns when no provider ran, or skipping the read would wipe the very fields it is meant to protect. (1) alone changes `Etag` (dto_service.rs:1260 hashes DateLastSaved) and the `minDateLastSaved` query filters on every DTO in the API, so it is a server-wide change needing its own batch and its own perf run. Recorded here rather than hidden: the journey deliberately forces the scan and waits for it, so this stays a deterministic red instead of a race whose colour depends on when the suite happened to run.

POST /Items/RemoteSearch/MusicArtist.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): the fetcher gate is ported and correct, but Ferrofin cannot RESOLVE a MusicArtist's library, so the gate is inert for that one kind. `LocalProviderManager::remote_search` now runs the C# `CanRefreshMetadata` chain (v10.11.8 ProviderManager.cs:801-830 -> :462-491 -> BaseItemManager.cs:26-46) and resolves the owning library through the reference item's `TopParentId`. Ferrofin's MusicArtist rows are materialized BY NAME out of `ItemValues` (library_scan.rs `item_values_of`, Artist=0/AlbumArtist=1), so they carry TopParentId='', ParentId='', Path=NULL and no `AncestorIds` row — verified directly in the lab DB for all three fixture artists. With no library resolvable the gate falls through permissive, so the GATED leg of the reads probe (ItemId=<own Artist>, IncludeDisabledProviders=false, against a Music library whose TypeOptions[MusicArtist].MetadataFetchers is []) answers with the MusicBrainz hit where Jellyfin answers []. Jellyfin's MusicArtist IS the artist DIRECTORY (measured: Path=/media/synth/music/Artist 01, ParentId=<Music library>), which is what makes `LibraryManager.GetCollectionFolders` (LibraryManager.cs:2262-2303) find the collection folder by path. The UNGATED leg of the same row diffs byte-identical, so the search itself is right; only the reference-item resolution is missing. Fix, in order of faithfulness: (1) give the materialized MusicArtist row its artist directory as `Path` (plus the owning library's TopParentId/ParentId) so the existing resolution works and `/Artists` stops serving Path:null — a library_scan change on the perf-gated path, needing its own batch and its own perf run; or (2) add a path-prefix fallback to `LocalProviderManager::library_options_for`, which only helps once (1) supplies the path. Same root cause as the separately observed `GET /Users/{userId}/Items?IncludeItemTypes=MusicArtist&Recursive=true` returning [] on Ferrofin and 3 on Jellyfin.
